relation: PART — coverage against the whole script
note: Armenian values 36 of 36 classical letters — the whole classical alphabet is the table (the 2 medieval additions stand outside it, OPEN). Halehame values 26 first forms of 202 classical signs (26/202); its labiovelar columns and later-added bases carry no value in any source.

relation: PART — the axis beyond the table
note: Armenian extends by MORE LETTERS (the thousands class) and by the OVERLINE: a line over a letter multiplies it — by 10,000 per Wikipedia and MELA (overlined Ա = 10,000; overlined Ջ = 9,000,000), by 1,000 per Omniglot (overlined Ժ = 10,000; overlined Ռ = 1,000,000). THE FACTOR IS DISPUTED IN THE SOURCES; neither is implemented. Halehame extends by the ORDER MULTIPLIER: a form at order n at n x its base, the printed grid reaching 5600 — printed entire, its use unexhibited.

relation: AGREE — the zero coordinate
note: Neither table has a zero: Armenian — "There is no symbol for zero" (Wikipedia, on its face); missing powers are simply not written. Halehame — no zero value in the folk table. Both are zero-less additive systems.

relation: PART — attestation depth (the control case itself)
note: Armenian: the designed alphabet's own numeral system, in manuscript use for era dating in colophons (MELA documents the practice; era epoch AD 552, years written ԹՎ + numerals) — three modern witnesses read entire agree on all 36 cells, a scholarly manual's examples agree on the 12 cells they exhibit. Halehame: a living folk-magical enumeration, published modernly, antiquity undated in every source, register expressly not liturgical. Same class-law shape; opposite attestation depth.
